story.conflict: A retired father must reclaim a say in his future when his son's worry about care becomes an excuse to make a life-changing decision behind his back.
story.hook: My brother emptied Dad's house during his retirement party. He'd booked a care-home room Dad didn't know about.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF DAD DESERVED A SAY
story.premise: A son empties his father's house during the father's retirement party and books him a care-home room without asking him.
story.punchline: The watch was a retirement gift. His house wasn't.
story.script: Dad still had his retirement watch in its box when we pulled up beside the moving truck. His armchair was inside it. He asked my brother, Paul, what was happening. Paul said Dad wouldn't need to worry about cooking or stairs anymore. Dad walked into the house and saw the empty rooms. He asked why nobody had mentioned moving. Paul said he'd known Dad would argue, and it was easier while everyone was at the party. Dad put the watch on the kitchen counter. He said he'd asked for help fixing the handrail, not for somebody to pack up his life. Paul said he'd already paid a deposit and taken time off to arrange everything. I asked why Dad was hearing about it after his furniture was gone. Paul said he'd been the one answering calls when Dad needed something. Dad said that was true, and he was willing to discuss getting more help. But Paul hadn't brought him a choice. He'd brought him a moving date. Dad asked the movers to put his things back. Paul said canceling would waste money. Dad said they'd talk about that too, after he had somewhere to sit. I stayed while they unloaded. Paul picked up the watch and asked whether Dad wanted it. Dad said yes, but he wasn't ready to thank him for the other present. The watch was a retirement gift. His house wasn't.
story.twist: The son's plan is presented as a thoughtful present, but the father has been excluded from deciding what help he actually needs.

youtube.description: Dad thinks the party marks the end of his working life. His son has arranged another change without telling him.
youtube.title: The Moving Truck After Dad's Retirement Party

story.conflict: A mother must own a false promise instead of treating her son's body as the solution to her fear for her brother.
story.hook: I volunteered my son's kidney without his permission. When he said no, I asked how he could let his uncle down.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF LOVE STILL NEEDS PERMISSION
story.premise: A mother volunteers her adult son's kidney for his uncle and pressures him to donate before she has even asked his permission.
story.punchline: That was something I could offer.
story.script: We were at dinner when my brother thanked Alex for being willing to help. Alex put his fork down and asked what he meant. I'd told the family he would be a donor before I'd even asked him. When Alex said I couldn't offer his kidney, I called him selfish. He asked whether I'd wanted an answer or just a yes. I said we couldn't leave his uncle without hope. My brother asked when Alex and I had discussed it. We hadn't. I'd assumed he would agree. Alex said I'd turned a decision about his body into a test of whether he loved us. I started explaining how much his uncle had done for him. My brother stopped me. He'd thought Alex had come to me with the idea. He said he hadn't asked me to promise something that wasn't mine. I told him I had been wrong to say a donation was settled. I didn't even know whether it was possible. Then I told the others that Alex hadn't broken a promise. I had made one for him. He asked whether I still wanted him at dinner if his answer stayed no. I said yes. He stayed, but he didn't pick his fork up straight away. I wanted to explain that I'd only been trying to help. Instead, I asked whether he wanted his plate warmed. That was something I could offer.
story.twist: The uncle believed the son had offered voluntarily, leaving the mother responsible for correcting a hope she created.

youtube.description: The uncle believes his nephew has offered to help. The mother who made that promise has not asked her son.
youtube.title: The Promise Made Over His Dinner Plate

story.conflict: An artist must choose between a lucrative sale and correcting a death story that is already hurting his family.
story.hook: I found my obituary in the gallery selling my paintings. The owner said being dead made my work worth more.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THAT SALE COST TOO MUCH
story.premise: An artist discovers his gallery has announced his death to increase painting prices, then must face his own brief agreement to keep the lie going.
story.punchline: The lie hadn't stayed entirely his.
story.script: My photograph was beside a sign saying final collection. Victor pulled me away from the doorway before the buyers saw me. He said he'd doubled the prices and would give me a bigger share if I stayed out of sight. I should have told him to stop. Instead, I asked how much. More than I'd earned from the last exhibition. I agreed to stay upstairs while he finished with a buyer. Then my phone rang. Mum had received a condolence message from someone who'd seen the display. She asked where I was and whether I was safe. I said I was fine. She asked why the gallery was telling people otherwise. I looked at the unfinished painting I'd brought with me, the one I'd promised her. Victor came upstairs and told me the buyer was ready to pay. I asked whether the buyer thought there would never be another painting. He said that was the point. I went downstairs and introduced myself. I said I was alive and explained the price had been raised because of a lie. The buyer canceled the purchase. Victor said I'd cost us both money. I called Mum back and told her I was coming over. I wanted to blame the gallery. But I had to tell her why I hadn't answered her question sooner. The lie hadn't stayed entirely his.
story.twist: The gallery starts the lie, but the artist's willingness to stay hidden for a larger payment makes him responsible for part of its harm.

youtube.description: The artist discovers why his paintings suddenly cost more. Then the gallery owner offers him a share of the lie.
youtube.title: The Gallery's Final Collection

story.conflict: A passenger must refuse to become a stranger's excuse for abandoning a wedding and put the decision back with the groom.
story.hook: My taxi driver took me to his wedding instead of my hotel. Then he asked me to object so he wouldn't have to say no.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF HE NEEDED TO SPEAK HIMSELF
story.premise: A taxi driver diverts a passenger's hotel journey to his own wedding and asks the passenger to object so he can avoid telling the bride he wants out.
story.punchline: His bride said she wasn't making his announcement for him, either.
story.script: He parked outside a hall and took a jacket from the passenger seat. I reminded him where I was going. He said he needed one favor first, and he'd give me the fare back. His bride was waiting by the doors. She asked who I was. He said I had something important to tell her. I told her I'd booked a taxi to my hotel. She asked what was going on. He whispered that I only needed to say the wedding shouldn't happen. I asked why he couldn't tell her himself. He said his father would never forgive him for backing out. The bride heard that. She asked whether he was planning to marry her because he was scared of his dad. He said I was making a simple request sound terrible. I told her he'd offered me my fare back to stop the ceremony for him. She asked him whether he actually wanted to be there. He looked at me again. I said I couldn't answer that. He finally told her he couldn't go through with it. She took a step away and said she wasn't marrying somebody who needed a passenger to tell her that. I called another taxi. Before it arrived, he asked whether I'd explain things to the guests. His bride said she wasn't making his announcement for him, either.
story.twist: The groom's fear of disappointing his family does not make either the passenger or the bride responsible for delivering his refusal.

youtube.description: The passenger books a ride to a hotel. The driver wants help escaping a wedding he has not called off.
youtube.title: The Wedding at the End of His Taxi Ride
